desc: World's largest industrial real estate investment trust, leasing logistics warehouses to retailers, logistics operators and manufacturers in many countries.
markets: Warehouses across the Americas, Europe and Asia, leased to retailers, logistics firms and manufacturers.
rationale: Global B2B landlord with a customer base of major brands; hospitality and customer entertainment value, but no consumer product.

name: J&T Express
desc: Express delivery company operating a franchised parcel network across Southeast Asia, China, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa.
markets: Parcel networks in Southeast Asia, China, Brazil, Mexico, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Fast-growing consumer-facing courier with emerging-market expansion; rivals such as DHL already sponsor F1, giving a clear logistics angle.

name: Big Brand Tire & Service
desc: Tire and auto service retailer with dozens of stores in California and the western US selling tires, wheels and repairs.
markets: Stores in California and other western US states; no operations outside the United States.
rationale: Regional US tire retailer with a clear product tie-in, but limited budget and no international reach.

name: BigBasket
desc: Online grocery and supermarket business offering scheduled and quick delivery of fruit, vegetables and household goods in many Indian cities.
markets: Serves consumers in Indian cities only; no international operations known.
rationale: Large Indian consumer brand with marketing budget but domestic focus; weak F1 fit despite its Tata group backing.
changed: Majority acquired by Tata Digital in 2021
f1: Group link only: Tata Communications, in the same Tata Group, is an F1 partner

name: Coca-Cola Consolidated
desc: Largest independent Coca-Cola bottler in the US, producing and distributing Coca-Cola products and other beverages in several states.
markets: Bottles and distributes drinks across the United States only.
rationale: US territorial bottler bound by franchise agreements with little scope for global sponsorship; weak F1 fit.

name: Cosan
desc: Brazilian holding company with stakes in fuels, rail logistics, gas distribution and lubricants, including the Raizen joint venture with Shell.
markets: Holdings serve Brazil, including Raizen, Rumo railways and Compass gas distribution.
rationale: Brazilian conglomerate with energy and logistics brands; Raizen's Shell link gives a motorsport angle, but a holding company.
f1: Joint venture Raizen uses the Shell brand in Brazil; Shell is an F1 partner

name: Mitsui & Co
desc: Tokyo-based general trading company founded in 1876 with businesses in energy, metals, machinery, chemicals, food, healthcare and mobility.
markets: Operates in about 60 countries across Asia, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Global conglomerate with mobility and energy interests and Japanese market links; strong B2B hospitality use but diffuse brand.

name: Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane
desc: Italy's state-owned railway group running passenger rail through Trenitalia, rail infrastructure through RFI and other transport businesses.
markets: Passenger and infrastructure operations mainly in Italy, with some rail businesses elsewhere in Europe.
rationale: State rail group with a consumer brand and Italian Grand Prix home markets, but public-sector procurement limits sponsorship appetite.
parent: Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance

name: HelloFresh
desc: Meal-kit company delivering boxes of recipes and pre-portioned ingredients to subscribers under HelloFresh and related brands.
markets: Sells in the US, Canada, Europe, Australia, New Zealand and Japan.
rationale: Consumer subscription brand with heavy marketing and customer acquisition in several F1 markets; strong fit for audience reach.

name: Aramex
desc: Courier and logistics company founded in 1982 offering express delivery, freight forwarding, warehousing and e-commerce fulfilment worldwide.
markets: Operates across the Middle East, Africa, Asia and Europe, with offices in North America.
rationale: Regional courier and direct rival of F1 partner DHL, based in a major F1 hub with strong brand marketing.
changed: Acquired by AD Ports Group (offer launched 2024)

name: Transnet
desc: South Africa's state-owned freight transport company operating the national freight rail network, ports and pipelines.
markets: Rail, ports and pipelines serving South African trade; limited operations elsewhere in Africa.
rationale: State logistics monopoly with financial and operational problems and no consumer marketing; weak F1 fit.

name: Agility
desc: Logistics and supply chain group providing freight forwarding, warehousing, industrial parks and infrastructure services, with roots in Kuwait.
markets: Operates in the Middle East, Africa and Asia with warehousing and industrial real estate.
rationale: Gulf logistics and infrastructure group with a B2B focus; rivals like DHL sponsor F1, but limited marketing culture.

name: Akiem
desc: Paris-based European rail leasing company and one of the leading lessors of locomotives to rail operators and freight companies.
markets: Leases locomotives to rail and freight operators across Europe.
rationale: Business-to-business locomotive lessor with no consumer marketing and rail operators as customers; weak F1 fit.

name: Costamare
desc: Owner and charterer of containerships leased to liner companies such as MSC, with dry bulk vessels held separately.
markets: Containerships chartered to global liner companies; headquartered in Monaco, not Germany.
rationale: B2B shipowner with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite Monaco base.

name: Global Partners
desc: Master limited partnership storing, distributing and marketing petroleum products, renewable fuels, natural gas and propane, and operating gas stations.
markets: Terminals and fuel stations in the northeastern United States and other US regions.
rationale: Regional US fuel distributor with retail brands; limited international reach, though motorsport fuel and branding links are possible.
f1: Operates Gulf-branded US fuel business; Gulf Oil International is a separate F1 partner, direct group link not confirmed

name: Motiva
desc: Brazilian mobility and infrastructure concession company, formerly CCR, operating toll roads, airports and urban rail and metro lines.
markets: Concessions mainly in Brazil serving motorists and rail and airport users.
rationale: Brazilian concession operator with consumer touchpoints and a Sao Paulo Grand Prix home market, but regulated and domestic.
changed: Rebranded from CCR to Motiva in 2025

name: SmartStop Self Storage
desc: Self-storage real estate investment trust owning and operating more than 200 self-storage facilities in the United States and Canada.
markets: Facilities in the United States and Canada serving consumers and businesses.
rationale: North American storage landlord with consumer brand but local business; weak F1 fit.

name: WestConnex
desc: Sydney motorway project delivering the M4, M8 and M5 tunnel links, built for the state government, now privately owned.
markets: Toll road network in Sydney, Australia, serving local motorists.
rationale: Single toll road asset with no consumer brand to market; no clear F1 case.
changed: Sold to a Transurban-led consortium in 2018

name: JD Logistics
desc: Logistics arm of JD.com providing warehousing, express delivery, freight and supply chain technology to JD.com and third-party customers.
markets: Network concentrated in China, with overseas warehouses and cross-border services in Europe, the US and Asia.
rationale: Brand-led Chinese logistics firm expanding abroad; rivals DHL and CEVA already sponsor F1, giving a clear logistics angle.

name: Getir
desc: Turkish ultra-fast grocery delivery company founded in 2015, delivering groceries and food in minutes from dark stores under Getir brands.
markets: Operations are centred on Turkey after it pulled out of several European and US markets.
rationale: Consumer delivery brand with marketing appetite but refocused on Turkey after retrenchment; weak to moderate fit.
changed: Withdrew from UK, Germany, Netherlands and US markets in 2024

name: Stord
desc: US commerce enablement company providing fulfilment, warehousing, freight and software for e-commerce and consumer brands.
markets: Warehouse network and software serving brands in the United States; international activity is not confirmed.
rationale: B2B fulfilment provider with limited brand budget and US focus; weak F1 fit.

name: United Parcel Service
desc: World's largest package delivery company, delivering packages and freight and offering logistics and supply chain services in over 200 countries.
markets: Delivers across North America, Europe, Asia and beyond with a large airline and ground network.
rationale: Global logistics brand whose rival DHL is an F1 partner; strong B2B hospitality and logistics showcase potential.

name: Ninja Van
desc: Singapore-founded last-mile logistics and courier company delivering e-commerce parcels and cross-border shipments across Southeast Asia.
markets: Parcel networks in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines.
rationale: Growing Southeast Asian courier with consumer-facing brand; Singapore Grand Prix home, and rival DHL sponsors F1.

name: Rohlik Group
desc: Czech online grocery delivery group operating Rohlik.cz, Knuspr, Kifli, Gurkerl and Sezamo in several European countries.
markets: Operates in the Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Austria, Italy and Spain.
rationale: European consumer grocery brand with expansion plans, but an operations-heavy business with limited sponsorship culture; weak to moderate fit.

name: Detroit Manufacturing Systems
desc: Detroit-based automotive manufacturing and logistics services company; products and current status are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Detroit serving the automotive sector; international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Unconfirmed automotive supplier with limited marketing profile and no verified international activity; weak F1 fit.

name: JOKR
desc: Quick-commerce grocery company operating an online supermarket that delivers groceries in minutes from dark stores in Brazil.
markets: Focused on Brazil after earlier launches in the US, Mexico and other Latin American countries.
rationale: Small delivery startup with limited budget and a Brazil-only focus; weak F1 fit.

name: Royal Mail
desc: UK national postal and parcel operator delivering letters and parcels to every address six days a week, including Parcelforce Worldwide.
markets: Delivers within the UK, with international mail and parcels handled through partners and Parcelforce.
rationale: Postal operator with strong consumer recognition but UK focus and cost pressure; limited F1 logic.
changed: Parent acquired by EP Group in 2025

name: Genesee & Wyoming
desc: Owner of short line and regional freight railroads in North America, Australia and Europe, hauling industrial and commodity freight.
markets: Railroads in North America, Australia and Europe serving industrial and commodity shippers.
rationale: B2B freight rail operator with no consumer brand and industrial shippers as customers; weak F1 fit.
changed: Acquired by Brookfield Infrastructure and GIC in 2019
